source.citation: Kachanov, Mark (1987). Elastic solids with many cracks: A simple method of analysis. International Journal of Solids and Structures 23(1), 23-43.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF), tables read on the page images
transcription.note: Table 1: two equal collinear cracks (-1,-k) and (k,1) under a remote tension normal to them; K_I at the inner tip x = k and at the outer tip x = 1, divided by K_I0 = p sqrt(pi (1 - k)/2), the factor of an isolated crack of the same length. Table 2: a periodic row of collinear cracks of length 2l and period h, K_I/K_I0 with K_I0 = p sqrt(pi l). The 'exact' columns are quoted by the article from Tada, Paris and Irwin, The Stress Analysis of Cracks Handbook (1973), not read here; the 'method' columns are the article's eqs (6) and (9).

notes: The article states the errors of its method in percent beside each row; they are not stored, being the relative differences of the two columns.
